b.label: GEIPAN - Groupe d'Études et d'Informations sur les Phénomènes Aérospatiaux Non identifiés

edges.label: GEIPAN is a unit of CNES at Toulouse
edges.note: The French office has been hosted inside the national space agency continuously since 1977, an arrangement Norlain called unique in the world.

edges.label: French private defence committee
edges.note: The report states its own legal status on its title page: 'COMETA, an association governed by the Law of July 1, 1901', the French statute for non-profit associations. Its foreword, by former CNES chairman Andre Lebeau, and the account by the former director of the Institut des Hautes Etudes de Defense Nationale place its formation in the IHEDN Auditors Association after General Denis Letty approached IHEDN in March 1995.

b.label: Les OVNI et la Défense: à quoi doit-on se préparer? (COMETA report, July 1999)

edges.label: produced the 1999 report
edges.note: Published as a special issue of VSD in July 1999 and delivered to Prime Minister Lionel Jospin.

edges.label: IHEDN origin; delivered to the Prime Minister
edges.note: TIER 3. What the report establishes: General Norlain, then director of the IHEDN, writes that 'when General Letty visited me in March 1995 at my office at IHEDN to explain to me his project for creating a new fact-finding committee on UFOs, I assured him of my interest and referred him to the management of the IHEDN Auditors Association'. What it does not establish is the city. Paris appears nowhere in the report in connection with COMETA; the IHEDN sits at the Ecole militaire in Paris, but that is knowledge brought to the document rather than read from it. Nor does the report record delivery to the head of government - it says only that its authors believed 'sufficient questions of national interest are raised for the Chief of State and the Prime Minister to be provided with this information.'

edges.label: adopts Hynek's Blue Book-era classification
edges.note: COMETA states that the strangest category D cases 'are generally labeled CE3s (close encounters of the third kind) according to the classification proposed by Professor A. Hynek, an astronomer and consultant to the USAF, within the context of the Blue Book Project'. A committee of retired French flag officers adopting Blue Book's own consultant's taxonomy is the inheritance this edge records.

edges.label: dedicated appendix on Roswell and disinformation
edges.note: COMETA's Appendix 5 is titled 'The Roswell Affair - Disinformation'. A committee of retired French flag officers treating Roswell as a subject requiring an appendix in a defence study is itself part of what this edge records; the report's own framing places it under disinformation rather than under evidence.

b.label: SETKA-AN / SETKA-MO (later Galaktika, then Gorizont) - Soviet state anomalous phenomena programme

edges.label: cites Soviet statistical distributions as comparable
edges.note: TIER 3, INFERENTIAL. COMETA records that 'statistical studies in the USSR yielded distributions comparable to those determined by Claude Poher, the first head of GEPAN, from some 200 French cases, or 1,000 cases worldwide.' The report does not name the Setka programme, or any Soviet programme, anywhere in that passage. That the studies it refers to are Setka's is inference from the period and the scale, not citation, and this edge should not be read as COMETA citing Setka.

a.label: GEIPAN - Groupe d'Études et d'Informations sur les Phénomènes Aérospatiaux Non identifiés

edges.label: shared IHEDN lineage; SEPRA head contributed
edges.note: COMETA's introduction records the shared parentage: 'In 1976, a committee of the Institut des Hautes Etudes de Defense Nationale (IHEDN) chaired by General Blanchard of the Gendarmerie Nationale opened the unidentified flying objects file. The objective: to make proposals for organizing research and the collection of data on these phenomena. The goal was achieved, because the recommendations of this committee were followed in the creation of the Groupe d'Etude des Phenomenes Aerospatiaux Non Identifies (GEPAN).' COMETA then rests its own report on GEPAN/SEPRA's casework by name.
